triggers.grounds: Well calibrated; the band is neither masking a bad warrant nor under-stating a strong one. The cluster's entire cohesion warrant is the run דִּבְרֵ֥י פִי (oshb:Eccl.10.12, tier: byte) recurring inside דִּבְרֵי פִ֖יהוּ (oshb:Eccl.10.13, tier: byte), and the row states that relation at its true tier: re-collated, the two runs are NOT byte-equal, the accent-stripped 10:12 run IS a leading substring of the accent-stripped 10:13 run, and the reverse containment is false - exactly as written. The row's byte reason for the tier split also re-derives: the construct noun at oshb:Eccl.10.12 carries a cantillation mark (U+05A5) and the same noun at oshb:Eccl.10.13 carries none, and since the staged extract is maqaf-free the difference is real accentuation, not maqaf loss. Object-named sweeps: word-bound adjacency of the two elements stands at 1 verse book-wide (Eccl.10.12 only, because 10:13's second element is the token פִ֖יהוּ), the contiguous-skeleton form at 2 verses book-wide (Eccl.10.12, Eccl.10.13). So the cohesion is one shared word-bound content token plus a contained second element - precisely the 'cluster cohesion thinner than two shared content tokens' case the book registers as an expected low-confidence region, and device_notes states that thinness instead of hiding it. Both edges also hold: Eccl.10.13 and Eccl.10.14 share 0 word-bound skeleton tokens, and the forward rejection names the right absent object (the construct phrase, not the word-root, which does recur at oshb:Eccl.10.14 in דְבָרִ֑ים). No whole-chapter cap is engaged.

findings.claim: The sentence that carries the cluster decision labels the recurrence word-bound while attaching to it a contiguous-substring sweep digit.
findings.grounds: Re-swept with the count object named: word-bound adjacency of דִּבְרֵ֥י פִי (oshb:Eccl.10.12, tier: byte) as two whole tokens returns 1 verse book-wide (Eccl.10.12 only), because the second element at oshb:Eccl.10.13 is the token פִ֖יהוּ and not the bare form; the cited digit '(sweep: 2 verses book-wide, both inside this span)' belongs to the contiguous consonantal-substring object (Eccl.10.12, Eccl.10.13), which is the sweep that actually returns 2. Under a word-bound object there is no recurrence at all, so 'word-bound' and the digit cannot both describe the same sweep. The row's own two preceding sentences state the containment correctly ('a contained leading substring ... at accent-stripped tier ... does not collate ... in reverse'), so this reads as a summary-label slip that the same field contradicts, not as a misleading evidence claim; the seam and the cluster both survive on the disclosed containment.
findings.proposed_change: In boundary_rationale replace 'This word-bound construct-phrase recurrence' with a construction-named form, e.g. 'This construct-phrase recurrence, word-bound at Eccl.10.12 and contained inside the suffixed form at Eccl.10.13,' leaving the (sweep: 2 verses book-wide) digit attached to the contiguous-substring object. Field repair only; no span, seam or unit_type change.

findings.claim: observed_substrate_signals carries the device-inventory filename in row prose.
findings.grounds: The signal reads 'catchword-staging texture for this chapter, per eccl_device_inventory (ch10 catchword staging)'. The book's register law bars inventory and tool filenames from row prose outright, and the filename is avoidable: the immediately preceding row (span Eccl.10.10-Eccl.10.11) writes the same staging signal as a bare taxonomy key, 'sentence_zone_texture (ch10 catchword staging)'. The underlying staging digit is right - the staged inventory records ch 10 catchword adjacency at 3 shared pairs of 19 adjacent pairs, the book's lowest - so this is disclosure/register class with no evidence effect. The staged cross-row templating gate is GREEN over this batch, but its worst-reuse list is this very phrase, shared verbatim with the row at Eccl.11.1-Eccl.11.6.
findings.proposed_change: Rewrite the signal as a bare taxonomy key, e.g. 'sentence_zone_texture (ch10 catchword staging)', dropping the filename. Field repair only.

triggers.grounds: The stated reason for the band is not a boundary reason at all, and the row says so itself. device_notes reads 'Held at medium_low chiefly for the continuation-paragraph fold hazard flagged for this verse, which requires care in any WEB quotation spanning it, not for the boundary call itself'. The fold is real - the staged WEB verse map flags this verse with a continuation paragraph, and the staged device inventory lists exactly two such WEB verses book-wide - but the WEB paragraph layer is tier-4 metadata that is never boundary evidence and never counterevidence, so it cannot licitly set a boundary confidence. The boundary itself is byte-clean: the verse sits inside the ruled sentence zone where single_saying is the default; Eccl.10.13 and Eccl.10.14 share 0 word-bound skeleton tokens; the only cross-seam device forward is the negated knowing root, לֹא יֵדַ֤ע (oshb:Eccl.10.14, tier: byte) against תְּיַגְּעֶ֑נּוּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר (oshb:Eccl.10.15, tier: byte), 2 shared word-bound skeleton tokens, and it is disclosed and declined; and the structurally identical following row (span Eccl.10.15-Eccl.10.15, single_saying, same zone default, same disclosed knowing-root texture) ships at high. The confidence is therefore under-stated, on a tier-4 ground - a defect under the low-band test, not honest calibration.

findings.claim: The row's confidence band is driven by a tier-4 WEB paragraph-layer hazard rather than by any doubt about the seam, under-stating a byte-clean zone-default boundary.
findings.grounds: device_notes names the continuation-paragraph fold as the chief and only reason for medium_low while expressly disclaiming any effect on the boundary call, and no other element of the row supports a low band: the opening splice וְהַסָּכָ֖ל יַרְבֶּ֣ה דְבָרִ֑ים re-collates at oshb:Eccl.10.14 at byte tier, the staged WEB-quote check passes GREEN over both curly-quoted runs, the staged refs-mirror and citation checks pass GREEN, the verse carries no ketiv/qere (the staged inventory's ch-10 K/Q sites are MT 10:3, MT 10:10 and MT 10:20), and the verse is outside the book's registered ch-10 low-confidence region, which is 10:15-10:20 for the K/Q at 10:20 and its syntax. Inside boundary_rationale the same fold is handled correctly, as a pure quotation-hygiene disclosure ('the quoted spans above are taken from within v.14's own folded text and do not reach across the fold'); the defect is only that the same tier-4 fact is then allowed to set the confidence field.
findings.proposed_change: Re-derive the band from bytes and either (a) raise it to match the identically-warranted following row at Eccl.10.15-Eccl.10.15, keeping the fold in device_notes as the quotation-hygiene disclosure it already is, or (b) if a genuine boundary doubt exists, state it in byte terms (the shared negated-knowing texture with the following verse) instead of the paragraph fold. Confidence/device_notes repair only; span, seam and unit_type unchanged.

triggers.grounds: Honest, and the band sits on a region the book itself registers. All three named binders re-derive exactly, each at the tier the row claims and no higher. (i) לֹ֣א תֵדַ֔ע (oshb:Eccl.11.2, tier: byte) against לֹ֤א תֵדַע֙ (oshb:Eccl.11.5, tier: byte): byte-unequal, accent-stripped EQUAL - the tier the row names; contiguous-skeleton sweep of the form returns 2 verses book-wide (Eccl.11.2, Eccl.11.5). (ii) אֵֽינְךָ֤ יוֹדֵ֨עַ֙ (oshb:Eccl.11.5, tier: byte) against אֵֽינְךָ֨ יוֹדֵ֜ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6, tier: byte): byte-unequal AND accent-stripped-unequal, skeleton-equal only - again exactly the tier the row names; sweep returns 2 verses book-wide (Eccl.11.5, Eccl.11.6). (iii) עַל הָאָֽרֶץ (oshb:Eccl.11.2, tier: byte) against its oshb:Eccl.11.3 counterpart: word-bound adjacent pair = 7 verses book-wide (MT 5:1 = WEB 5:2, Eccl.8.14, Eccl.8.16, Eccl.10.7, Eccl.11.2, Eccl.11.3, Eccl.12.7) and Eccl.11.2/Eccl.11.3 is indeed the only adjacent pair among them - both halves of the claim true. The sowing-root binder likewise: contiguous-skeleton sweep returns 2 verses / 3 tokens book-wide, both inside the span, יִזְרָ֑ע (oshb:Eccl.11.4, tier: byte) and זְרַ֣ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6, tier: byte), and the row correctly refuses to call it a word-bound identity. The directive distribution holds too: no second-person directive stands anywhere in vv.3-5. Against that byte strength the row still holds medium_low, and the reason is legitimate and stated - the bread-on-waters crux at v.1 is a registered expected low-confidence region and device_notes cites exactly it. The span is also the book's own named admonition-unit candidate, and the whole-chapter cap is not engaged (6 of ch 11's 10 verses).

The matched string is 'that verse closes its own sentence zone (web:Eccl.10.20)'. 'Sentence zone' here is the book's ruled sentence-literature zone that ends at Eccl.10.20 - a genre designation carried by the book's own strategy and corroborated by the staged catchword-adjacency staging signal (ch 10 = 3 shared pairs of 19) - not a WEB sentence, punctuation, paragraph or poetry-line fact. No tier-4 layer is doing driver or corroboration work at this seam: the warrant standing beside it is a byte comparison, and it is true - oshb:Eccl.10.20 and oshb:Eccl.11.1 share exactly one word-bound skeleton token, the causal particle (כִּ֣י there, כִּֽי here, tier: byte at each). The same sentence explicitly refuses the tier-4 alternative ('Both outer bounds hold clean on content rather than chapter numbering'), and its forward-seam counterpart is likewise byte-true: oshb:Eccl.11.6 and oshb:Eccl.11.7 share exactly one word-bound skeleton token, the object marker (אֶת / אֶת, tier: byte at each). The trigger is a matcher artefact of the adjacent web: ref, not a tier-4 driver.

findings.claim: device_notes attaches the 20-verse ruach digit to 'the bare ruach word-bound form' and cites Eccl.11.5 as one of its two sites; the bare word-bound form stands at 13 verses book-wide, and Eccl.11.5 carries the definite form, not the bare one.
findings.grounds: Re-swept with the object named. Verses carrying the bare word-bound token ר֖וּחַ (oshb:Eccl.11.4, tier: byte): 13 book-wide (Eccl.1.14, 1.17, 2.11, 2.17, 2.26, 3.21, 4.4, 4.6, 4.16, 6.9, 7.8, 10.4, 11.4). Verses carrying ANY token built on that skeleton: 20 book-wide - which is the staged device inventory's own object, recorded there as 'verses containing any token carrying' the noun, count 20, and it is that inventory digit the row imported. The row's own observed_substrate_signals names the object correctly ('any-ruach word-bound form ... sweep: 20 verses book-wide'); device_notes then rewrites the same digit as 'the bare ruach word-bound form occurs at 20 verses book-wide'. The cited sites split the same way: oshb:Eccl.11.4 does carry ר֖וּחַ bare (tier: byte), but oshb:Eccl.11.5 carries הָר֔וּחַ (tier: byte), the definite form, so it is not an instance of the form device_notes names - 'these two ch-11 sites carry it' is false for the second site. The claim is framed as texture and expressly not adopted as a boundary device ('it stays texture, not a boundary device'), so no seam rests on it and no span moves; but the digit and its stated object do not match, and one of the two cited sites is wrong for the form named. This is the book's own named counting hazard (name the object, then count) landing inside a row that otherwise observes it scrupulously.
findings.proposed_change: In device_notes either restore the inventory's object ('any token carrying the wind/breath noun occurs at 20 verses book-wide') or keep the bare word-bound object and correct both the digit (13 verses book-wide) and the site list (Eccl.11.4 only), naming the definite form at Eccl.11.5 separately. Field repair only; observed_substrate_signals already carries the correct object and needs no change beyond the register fix below.

findings.claim: Four universal or exclusivity claims in the driver field carry no adjacent digit-bearing sweep citation; all four are byte-true.
findings.grounds: The staged universals checker returns 2 flags on this row after its tier dampener; a full pass of the field finds four digit-less claims, and each re-derives as true. (a) 'The three middle verses carry no second-person directive at all' - true, vv.3-5 carry none (v.5 carries second-person reference but no directive). (b) 'No byte warrant separates any internal seam that these three binders do not themselves cross' - an interpretive negative with no countable object; nothing in the bytes contradicts it. (c) 'the back seam shares with the preceding verse only a causal particle, a function word' - true: oshb:Eccl.10.20 and oshb:Eccl.11.1 share exactly 1 word-bound skeleton token, כִּ֣י / כִּֽי. (d) 'the forward seam shares with the following verse only the object marker' - true: oshb:Eccl.11.6 and oshb:Eccl.11.7 share exactly 1 word-bound skeleton token, אֶת / אֶת. Disclosure class only: the book's law requires the digit even where the claim holds, and the row's other exclusivity claims in the same field do carry theirs (the two 2-verse binder sweeps and the 7-verse on-the-earth sweep).
findings.proposed_change: Append shared-token digits to the two seam claims (e.g. 'only a causal particle (sweep: 1 shared word-bound token)') and a directive digit to the middle-verse claim. Field repair only; no evidence changes.

findings.claim: observed_substrate_signals carries the device-inventory filename in row prose.
findings.grounds: The signal reads 'catchword-staging texture for this chapter, per eccl_device_inventory (ch11 catchword staging, thin)'. The register law bars inventory and tool filenames from row prose, and the same signal is written filename-free elsewhere in the corpus. The staging characterisation itself is right - the staged inventory records ch 11 catchword adjacency at 2 shared pairs of 9 adjacent pairs, so 'thin' is accurate. Disclosure/register class; no evidence effect. The staged templating gate is GREEN for the batch, but its worst-reuse entries are this phrase, shared verbatim with the row at Eccl.10.12-Eccl.10.13.
findings.proposed_change: Rewrite as a bare taxonomy key, e.g. 'sentence_zone_texture (ch11 catchword staging, thin)'. Field repair only.

triggers.grounds: Honest calibration on a genuinely contested edge. The cohesion the row rests on re-derives at the strength it claims and no more: the rejoice root stands at both oshb:Eccl.11.8 and oshb:Eccl.11.9 (contiguous-skeleton sweep, 14 verses book-wide, these two among them), and the remember root stands at exactly one of the span's four verses, oshb:Eccl.11.8 (sweep, 7 verses book-wide; Eccl.11.7, Eccl.11.9 and Eccl.11.10 are not among them) - which is precisely what the row says, thinness included. The disclosed rivals are real, not decorative: the person register does shift across the 11:8/11:9 join (כִּ֣י אִם שָׁנִ֥ים הַרְבֵּ֛ה יִחְיֶ֥ה הָאָדָ֖ם (oshb:Eccl.11.8, tier: byte) is third-person against שְׂמַ֧ח בָּח֣וּר (oshb:Eccl.11.9, tier: byte) second-person), and the closing seam is genuinely crossed both by the imperative chain (שְׂמַ֧ח בָּח֣וּר at oshb:Eccl.11.9, וְהָסֵ֥ר at oshb:Eccl.11.10, וּזְכֹר֙ at oshb:Eccl.12.1, tier: byte at each) and by the youth-phrase catchword, whose shared skeleton prefix sweeps to exactly 2 verses book-wide (Eccl.11.9, Eccl.12.1) while each full attested form stands at 1 verse - so 'near-identical' is the right label and the '(sweep: 2 verses)' digit is true for the shared-prefix object. The book's law leaves the aging-allegory bounds writer-argued, so holding a low band at an edge the row itself shows to be crossed is calibration, not concealment. Not a whole-chapter span, and the row's own rejected alternative states the live split rather than burying it.

findings.claim: The row's own opening verse and back edge carry no original-language evidence: Eccl.11.7 is argued only from its WEB rendering, with no pointed splice, no tier label and no oshb: ref, and the preceding verse is never compared.
findings.grounds: In boundary_rationale every other verse of the span is spliced with a ref and a tier (oshb:Eccl.11.8, oshb:Eccl.11.9, oshb:Eccl.11.10, and oshb:Eccl.12.1 across the seam), while Eccl.11.7 - the row's first verse and the verse the back seam turns on - appears only as a curly-quoted WEB run plus the characterisation 'third-person reflection'; boundary_evidence_refs correspondingly lists oshb:Eccl.11.8, oshb:Eccl.11.9 and oshb:Eccl.12.1 but no oshb:Eccl.11.7 and no reference to the preceding verse. The book's engagement rule requires a pointed splice and tier label for every boundary-relevant original-language claim, and 'opens in third-person reflection' is exactly such a claim. The edge is nevertheless sound and the bytes for it exist: oshb:Eccl.11.6 and oshb:Eccl.11.7 share exactly one word-bound skeleton token, the object marker (אֶת / אֶת, tier: byte), and oshb:Eccl.11.7 carries הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ (tier: byte) outside the under-the-sun formula - the light-frame the row already names in observed_substrate_signals and the preceding row names in its forward-seam argument. So this is an evidence-completeness gap on a correct seam, not a false warrant; the staged refs-mirror check passes because nothing argued outside the span is left unmirrored.
findings.proposed_change: Splice the opening verse from its own bytes with a tier label and add oshb:Eccl.11.7 to boundary_evidence_refs - the light-frame noun at oshb:Eccl.11.7 is the natural candidate, since observed_substrate_signals already carries that signal - and state the back-edge token comparison against the preceding verse. Field and refs repair only; span, seam, unit_type and confidence unchanged.

triggers.grounds: Calibrated, and the band sits squarely on a registered low-confidence region. The spine re-derives exactly: עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹא (oshb:Eccl.12.1, tier: byte) and the forms spliced at oshb:Eccl.12.2 and oshb:Eccl.12.6 all reduce to one identical skeleton phrase, and a contiguous-skeleton sweep of it returns exactly 3 verses book-wide (Eccl.12.1, Eccl.12.2, Eccl.12.6), all three inside this span - so 'triple anaphora spining the poem' is byte-true and the three-way split the row rejects would cut that spine. The ketiv/qere claim checks out twice over: MT 12:6 is one of the 12 K/Q verses in the staged inventory, and the verse's own bytes carry the unpointed ketiv ירחק inline before the pointed qere יֵרָתֵק֙ (oshb:Eccl.12.6, tier: byte for both), whose middle consonants differ - so 'two distinct roots rather than one lexeme pointed two ways' is a byte fact, not a gloss. Rare lexemes at 12:4-6 together with that K/Q are exactly the region the book registers for a low band, and device_notes cites both. The closing splice re-collates whole at oshb:Eccl.12.7 at byte tier and the row stops at the ruled monologue/epilogue seam without straddling it. No fabricated mark classes appear (no selah, no special-letter claim); the staged mark and citation checks are GREEN. medium_low is honest, not a low-band label over a defective warrant.

findings.claim: The rejected alternative justifies itself with a cross-unit reference written in decision voice and carrying no verse anchor.
findings.grounds: It reads 'matching how the time-catalogue's internal repetition is held as one list unit'. The register law requires cross-row references to be verse-anchored, and this one names no verses; the catalogue is MT 3:1-3:8 = WEB 3:1-3:8 (identity numbering there, so a bare anchor would have been unambiguous). The underlying claim is true - the catalogue is the book's ruled single list unit, and its internal repetition is the 29 word-bound time-noun tokens the staged inventory records across those eight verses (1 at 3:1 and 4 in each of 3:2-3:8) - so under the register test this is a true claim merely phrased in decision voice, with no effect on the rejection's force or on the span.
findings.proposed_change: Verse-anchor and de-process the clause, e.g. 'matching the internal repetition that runs through Eccl.3.1-Eccl.3.8 without closing a unit at each recurrence'. Field repair only; the rejection stands.

triggers.grounds: Well calibrated, and the row's one hazardous digit is handled exactly right - this is the batch's cleanest counting discipline. The serial connective וְיֹתֵ֕ר (oshb:Eccl.12.9, tier: byte) recurs in the same word-bound form at oshb:Eccl.12.12; re-swept with the object named, that word-bound token stands at exactly 3 verses book-wide (Eccl.7.11, Eccl.12.9, Eccl.12.12), which is the digit and the site list the row cites, while a contiguous-substring sweep of the same letters returns 6 verses because the profit-noun וְיִתְר֥וֹן (oshb:Eccl.10.10, tier: byte) adds MT 5:8 = WEB 5:9, Eccl.7.12 and Eccl.10.10 - and the row pre-empts precisely that by naming the word-bound object and excluding 'the wider profit-noun family on the same root'. The spelling point is byte-true as well: the defective name-form קֹהֶ֖לֶת (oshb:Eccl.12.9, tier: byte) sweeps to 6 verses book-wide (Eccl.1.1, 1.2, 1.12, 7.27, 12.9, 12.10), including v.9-10 and excluding the preceding motto's plene definite form, and the row correctly demotes it to background texture rather than promoting it to seam evidence. Both outer edges are byte-quiet - oshb:Eccl.12.8/oshb:Eccl.12.9 and oshb:Eccl.12.11/oshb:Eccl.12.12 each share 0 word-bound skeleton tokens - the span is the book's own named epilogue unit, the row respects the ruled epilogue parent, and the verse-initial construct at Eccl.12.11 is correctly identified as a genitive rather than a header, the book's live header-versus-genitive hazard. The medium_low band is then held for a real and disclosed reason: the internal v.10/v.11 shift the row declines to promote, plus the long-disputed one-shepherd referent at מֵרֹעֶ֥ה אֶחָֽד (oshb:Eccl.12.11, tier: byte). Neither over- nor under-stated.
